policy: Source location, source type, study year and geographic/diagnostic scope must remain attached to every claim; no current site occurrence inferred from historic surveys or abstract-only descriptors.

records.label: Agusan Marsh comparative characters
records.text: A 2026 specimen-based account describes an olive-grey back, a vertebral stripe absent in most examined frogs, yellow bars on the inner hind limbs or groin, and no outer tarsal or fifth-toe flap compared with F. moodiei.
records.studyScope: Character combination attributed to examined Agusan Marsh vouchers. Stripe variable; not a validated all-island field key.

records.label: Observed wetland microhabitats
records.text: Examined Agusan Marsh frogs were reported along rice-field irrigation channels and in quiet pools beside creeks and rivers.
records.studyScope: Agusan Marsh locality observations, not a nationwide habitat preference or site occupancy prediction.

records.label: Philippine snake-key character
records.text: The published Philippine Trimeresurus key describes a red tail contrasting with a green body in life; other characters are necessary and colour alone cannot confirm an identification.
records.source: Leviton et al. (2019), Illustrated Key to the Snakes of the Philippines
records.sourceLocation: Genus Trimeresurus, Philippine species key, couplet 1a
records.studyScope: Key also uses hemipenes; do not handle this venomous snake for identification. Colour notes apply to living specimens and may vary.

records.label: Specimen-based scale comparison
records.text: A published comparative treatment reports 55–65 preanofemoral pores, 14–17 dorsal tubercle rows and snout–vent length up to 103.5 mm for Gekko gigante.
records.studyScope: Rösler et al. compile comparison with Brown & Alcala (1978) and Alcala (1986); measurements are specimen-based, not remotely confirmed by a photograph.

records.label: Revised stream-frog comparison
records.text: The 2017 revision reports male snout–vent lengths of 61.7–79.5 mm and a graded dark-to-light flank colour transition in sampled S. everetti, distinguishing its comparison series from S. acai.
records.sourceLocation: Table 3, comparison of Sanguirana acai and S. everetti
records.studyScope: Examined samples and taxonomic comparison; body size and flank gradient alone do not distinguish all Philippine Sanguirana. Former West Visayan everetti populations were reassigned to S. acai.

records.label: Published advertisement-call structure
records.text: The species' published male advertisement calls consist of paired calls with two notes each; part of the second note is amplitude-modulated and the calls contain multiple harmonics.
records.sourceLocation: DOST abstract of Brown et al., Advertisement calls of two endangered endemic Philippine frogs
records.studyScope: Acoustic structure from male calls at limestone localities in southern Negros; archived study abstract, not a quantified recognition threshold.

records.label: Observed limestone-crevice egg laying
records.text: A 2010 comparative limestone-frog description reports direct-developing eggs of P. spelaeus deposited in limestone crevices.
records.source: Siler et al. (2010), Zootaxa 2482:25–42, Platymantis biak description
records.sourceLocation: Natural history discussion, note on P. spelaeus egg deposition
records.studyScope: Observation attributed to C. D. Siler, not a measured egg count, seasonality estimate or study of nationwide nesting sites.

records.label: Measured understorey and canopy associations
records.text: A 2018 Northwest Panay field survey found detections positively associated with dense understorey at 1.5 m and dense canopy cover (model P values 0.001 and 0.003).
records.source: Mynott, Abrahams & Kerhoas (2021), Bird Conservation International 31:640–655
records.sourceLocation: Results, Habitat preference; 93 habitat plots, 31 sightings
records.studyScope: GLM for measured plots in Northwest Panay in 2018. Statistical associations are not a confirmed occupancy map for all of Panay or Negros.

records.label: Camera-trap effort and detections
records.text: The 2018 study recorded three camera-trap detections on separate days at one Northwest Panay location during 161 camera-days of sampling.
records.source: Mynott, Abrahams & Kerhoas (2021), Bird Conservation International 31:640–655
records.studyScope: Three detections at one camera location do not establish independent individuals or density; study effort was 161 camera-days.

records.label: Observed disturbance and salinity tolerance
records.text: The northern Sierra Madre survey reports live Philippine crocodiles in freshwater rivers, creeks and ponds, and in coastal riverine habitats with saline conditions in parts of Isabela.
records.sourceLocation: Species account, Crocodylus mindorensis, Isabela field records
records.studyScope: Observed habitats in Isabela, not a claim of broad marine tolerance or current persistence at every listed locality.

records.label: Historical mapped locality records
records.text: The published northern Sierra Madre survey documented crocodile observations in parts of Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, San Mariano, Benito Soliven and San Guillermo, Isabela.
records.sourceLocation: Species account, Crocodylus mindorensis, documented municipalities
records.studyScope: Historical field records from this survey. They are not live 2026 point occurrences and must not populate the app's local range filter.

records.label: 2012 Negros camera-trap context
records.text: A March–April 2012 survey in North Negros Natural Park photographed wild Visayan spotted deer during 185 camera-trap days, supporting occurrence in the park's forest interior at that time.
records.source: Oryx (2013), First images of the Visayan spotted deer and Visayan warty pig
records.sourceLocation: Fieldwork and results, North Negros Natural Park
records.studyScope: Detection of species during limited 2012 camera effort; no abundance or current site presence inferred.

records.label: Frugivory in original species description
records.text: The original 2010 species description characterizes Varanus bitatawa as a frugivorous forest monitor from the central and northern Sierra Madre.
records.studyScope: Described feeding guild and field context, not a quantified diet sample or evidence of current presence anywhere in the mapped forest.
